system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS alert activity is attributable in the endpoint telemetry to C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe (PID 4812), running as leo.martins.
The proxy records identify the updater's destination as updates.pixelforge-suite.com, which the provided environment context lists as PixelForge Suite's approved update service.

The observed updater connections recur at roughly five-minute intervals: 13:40:51, 13:45:21, 13:50:28, 13:55:32, 14:00:11, 14:05:36, and 14:10:35 UTC. The 13:45:21 attempt received proxy status 407; the other listed attempts received status 200.
There is also a 13:30:58 proxy tunnel to res.cdn.office.net, but the supplied records do not show that it is part of the PixelForge updater's recurring activity.

Separate SMB connections from the workstation to FILE-NWD-01 were recorded at 13:55:37 and 14:03:22, with corresponding FILE-NWD-01 logons recorded as ANONYMOUS LOGON. The available records do not establish what share or resource was accessed.

The workstation logged a WmiPrvSE.exe process, and DC-NWD-01 later made an inbound connection to the workstation on port 135. The records do not establish that these events are causally related or what operation occurred.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, byte counts, and durations, but do not expose the encrypted HTTPS payload.
The supplied records do not cover every minute in the review window, so they do not independently verify the full reported activity from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC.
The SMB records do not identify the accessed share or files, and the inbound port-135 records do not identify the remote operation or initiating user.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that the updater binary was authentic or that any update it obtained was safe; no hash or signature-validation evidence for pfupdater.exe is included.
The evidence does not establish what occurred over the SMB connections to FILE-NWD-01 or whether those connections were authorized.
The evidence does not establish whether the DC-NWD-01 connection to workstation port 135 was authorized or related to the WmiPrvSE.exe process.
The evidence does not establish that the PixelForge connections carried malicious content.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate the pfupdater.exe file signature and hash against the approved PixelForge release, and obtain update or application logs covering the connection times.
Collect FILE-NWD-01 SMB share-access and file-access auditing for the 13:55 and 14:03 connections.
Collect endpoint and DC records that identify the initiator, authentication context, and operation associated with the workstation's inbound port-135 connection and WmiPrvSE.exe activity.
